reviewer.role: independent read-only code proof and source I/O reviewer

scope: Design advice only. No production source, tests, Git state, network, connector, real Vault, or human relation review was mutated.

observed_boundary.existing_code_contract: code_evidence_contracts.py validates strict UTF-8 text metadata, normalized snippet hashes, a portable repository/full 40-hex commit/path origin, and content/proposal/manifest identities. The v1 origin cannot represent a 64-hex Git SHA-256 commit.
observed_boundary.existing_capture_io: staged_code_capture.py retains the prepared request, plan and payload file identities in one inspection and passes the caller-supplied payload to content-addressed transaction staging. It does not prove that payload bytes are the Git blob at the declared origin, and it has no multi-file Git lineage container.
observed_boundary.existing_file_safety: secure_io.read_regular_file uses no-follow parent/child reads, bounded reads and before/after identity checks; parse_strict_json rejects BOMs, duplicate keys, floats, non-finite constants and trailing data under the current JSON limits.
observed_boundary.prior_external_evidence: The prior source-git-show verification records SHA-1 blob IDs plus ordinary SHA-256 and size comparisons from an external read-only git show. It is evidence of an external procedure, not a public Python Git dependency or a multi-file observation contract.
observed_boundary.compatibility_implication: A SHA-256 repository commit must remain a 64-hex typed value in the proof and handoff. It cannot be truncated, re-encoded as a SHA-1, or silently placed in code-evidence-manifest.v1; SHA-256 source proof needs a successor manifest/binding or an explicit raw-capture-only state.

design_decision.purpose: Define a bounded local, uncompressed Git object proof bundle that an approved host or operator may supply as data, while the public Python verifier proves object self-consistency, one commit/tree lineage, complete requested target membership, and exact source bytes without running Git or using a network.
design_decision.trust_boundary: Git object hashes prove the supplied bytes are self-consistent objects under the selected object format. They do not prove that a hosting service owns the canonical repository, that a ref points to the commit, or that a paper officially claims the repository. Hosting assertions and independent relation review remain separate evidence.
design_decision.recommendation: Freeze the bundle, observation, and handoff schemas together. Do not dispatch implementation until SHA-256 compatibility, exact source spans, bundle snapshot rules, and target mode policy are resolved.
non_goals: No agent-side GitHub or Git fetcher, clone, archive download, remote ref lookup, shell command, or recursive repository traversal.
No compressed packfile, zlib loose-object transport, executable hook, config import, model loading, weight download, or arbitrary provider response parser.
No automatic officiality decision or publication. A host assertion is retained as an assertion and reviewed independently.
No mutation of code-evidence-manifest.v1, legacy locators, real Vault state, or existing capture transaction semantics in place.

root_layout.body_meaning: Each body file contains the exact uncompressed Git object body. The manifest records object_type and body_size; the verifier reconstructs type + ASCII space + decimal body_size + NUL + body bytes before hashing.
root_layout.root_policy: The root and every component are regular directories/files beneath the approved .work boundary. No component is followed through a symlink. The bundle is read as one retained local snapshot.

object_record.oid_rule: oid is lowercase and has exactly 40 hex characters for sha1 or 64 for sha256; every object in one bundle uses the selected object_format.
object_record.body_hash_rule: body_sha256 is ordinary SHA-256 over the exact uncompressed body bytes. framed_sha256 is ordinary SHA-256 over the Git object header and body. For object_format=sha256 the Git oid equals framed_sha256; for sha1 the oid is the separate SHA-1 digest of the same framed bytes.
object_record.deduplication: An OID appears at most once. A blob body may be referenced by several distinct logical target paths, but each target retains its own tree path proof.

commit_and_tree_proof.commit: The commit object is present and its first tree header resolves exactly to root_tree_oid. The parser retains parent OIDs and author/committer headers as data; it does not verify signatures or execute hooks.
commit_and_tree_proof.trees: The root tree and every intermediate tree needed by every requested path are present. Each raw tree body is hash-checked, parsed with Git's binary entry format, checked for valid names/no duplicate names/canonical ordering, and linked by the exact mode, entry name and child OID in the path walk.
commit_and_tree_proof.target_membership: A present target ends in a tree entry with the requested exact POSIX path and an allowed regular blob mode. A missing target retains the deepest proven parent tree and the exact missing edge; it never becomes a successful source target.
commit_and_tree_proof.object_set: The complete declared object set is exactly the commit, the path-walk trees, and the blob bodies for present blob targets. Unreferenced object records and omitted required path-walk objects refuse the bundle; unrelated entries inside a supplied tree body do not require their child objects.
commit_and_tree_proof.canonicalization: The manifest is strict UTF-8, BOM-free, duplicate-key-free, canonical JSON bytes, and contains no unknown fields. Object and target records are sorted by their canonical keys before bundle_sha256 is computed.

hosting_assertion.meaning: An optional bounded assertion that a provider/operator associated repository owner/name, commit_oid and perhaps a ref. It is not a cryptographic property of the Git object and cannot upgrade officiality.
rules: repository and commit_oid must equal the bundle values; a different host assertion is a typed repository/commit mismatch.
assertion_sha256 is SHA-256 of canonical assertion fields and only protects the retained assertion bytes. It is never substituted for oid, body_sha256, framed_sha256 or bundle_sha256.

No public Python code resolves provider URLs or validates provider signatures. A bundle without a hosting assertion is self-consistent but origin-unbound and cannot be presented as official source evidence.

hash_semantics.object_format: The request and bundle select exactly one of sha1 or sha256. Do not accept shortened OIDs, uppercase OIDs, mixed-format object records, or implicit algorithm negotiation.

separate_digests.git_oid: Git object identity under the selected object format, computed from the typed Git header plus exact body.
separate_digests.raw_sha256: Ordinary SHA-256 over source blob body bytes; this is the value carried into source capture and is distinct from the Git blob OID.
separate_digests.normalized_sha256: Existing UTF-8 LF-normalized source digest; it describes a derived text view and cannot replace raw_sha256 or git_oid.
separate_digests.framed_sha256: Ordinary SHA-256 over the Git typed header plus body; retained to make the object framing explicit even when the selected Git object format is SHA-1.
separate_digests.bundle_sha256: Ordinary SHA-256 over canonical manifest bytes plus the sorted declared object body bytes and their canonical relative names; no archive/compression implementation is implied.
separate_digests.hosting_assertion_sha256: Ordinary SHA-256 over the canonical retained host assertion. It proves only assertion-byte identity.

hash_semantics.sha256_transition: If a provider supplies a compatibility SHA-1 for a SHA-256 repository, retain it only in an explicitly typed compatibility field if a later schema freezes that rule. v1 must never use it as the primary commit/tree/blob identity or silently map a 64-hex commit into the legacy 40-hex field.
hash_semantics.raw_body_check: For every object, verify body file size, body_sha256, framed_sha256 and selected-format oid before parsing. For every blob target, require raw_sha256 == body_sha256 and preserve bytes byte-for-byte through the handoff.

observation_lineage.one_session_rule: One observation retains one request, one bundle snapshot, one repository, one object_format, one commit_oid and one root_tree_oid. All target records and path walks must come from that same retained bundle session.
observation_lineage.target_set: target_set_sha256 is SHA-256 over canonical sorted exact requested {ordinal, role, path, capability} records. Observation targets must equal the request set exactly: no omitted, duplicate, silently reordered, or extra target may be installed.
observation_lineage.retained_snapshot: Open the bundle root and all manifest/object files with no-follow, bounded retained I/O. Record directory/file identities and exact bytes, recheck them after hash/parsing and before returning, and fail closed on replacement, disappearance, mode change, size change or byte drift. A second target call must not be able to switch to another directory generation.

statuses.present: Exact requested path, commit/tree path walk, allowed mode/type, raw body and requested capability are proven.
statuses.missing: The path is absent at a proven parent tree; retain bounded inventory scope and no blob handoff.
statuses.inaccessible: The bundle or object cannot be read safely; retain the requested path and refusal reason.
statuses.mismatch: Repository, commit, format, tree, path, mode, type, OID or digest disagrees; retain requested and observed values.
statuses.unsafe: A symlink, submodule, unsupported tree/mode, unsafe bundle path or changed retained input is observed; no source handoff.

observation_lineage.completeness: OBSERVED_COMPLETE requires every requested target to be present with all required raw proof. Any missing, inaccessible, mismatch, unsafe, normalized-only or byte-limit target yields explicit partial/refusal and cannot be published as complete.
observation_lineage.order_independence: Target order and any connector arrival order do not affect canonical observation bytes. The verifier installs one complete observation only after the complete set and final retained-snapshot check pass.

target_admission.path_rules: Relative normalized POSIX paths only: no leading slash, empty/dot/dot-dot component, backslash, NUL, URL query/fragment, wildcard, encoded traversal, or recursive pattern. Compare exact requested path bytes; do not normalize an ambiguous path after observation.

git_modes.100644: Allowed regular non-executable blob for README, citation, license, implementation, configuration and entrypoint roles when the raw text capability is valid.
git_modes.100755: Allowed regular executable blob only for implementation or entrypoint roles after the request explicitly permits executable source. Preserve the mode in proof and handoff; existing code-evidence-manifest.v1 alone does not represent it.
git_modes.120000: Symlink entry; unsafe for v1. Retain bounded link-target bytes/oid only as refusal evidence and never dereference or hand off the target.
git_modes.160000: Gitlink/submodule entry; unsafe for v1. Do not treat the gitlink commit OID as a source blob or traverse the nested repository.
git_modes.040000_or_other: Tree is allowed only as an intermediate path-walk object; a requested target ending at a tree or any other mode refuses with a typed mode/type error.

target_admission.regular_file_rule: A present target must be Git type blob, mode 100644 or an explicitly permitted 100755, exact path match, body hash/OID match, and strict source capability validation. Local filesystem executable bits are never used to infer Git mode.
target_admission.duplicate_content_rule: Equal raw bytes or equal blob OIDs at distinct requested paths remain distinct logical targets and distinct origin paths. A content-addressed capture may deduplicate storage but cannot merge path evidence.
target_admission.normalized_only_rule: A normalized web excerpt or text-only connector result may be retained as normalized-only evidence, but it cannot satisfy raw blob proof, source handoff, config exact-span evidence, or an inspected Git source manifest.

source_handoff.payload_rule: The handoff payload is the exact blob body read from the retained proof bundle, not a checkout path or caller-supplied replacement. Verify raw_sha256 before placing it in the existing prepared/<sha256>.blob input.
source_handoff.sha1_compatibility: For object_format=sha1, a verified handoff may feed the existing code capture after retaining all new proof fields in the observation/handoff successor.
source_handoff.sha256_compatibility: For object_format=sha256, do not construct code-evidence-manifest.v1 because its commit contract is 40 hex. Freeze a successor manifest/binding carrying object_format and the 64-hex commit, or return a typed raw-capture-only result. Never truncate, hash, or substitute the commit.
source_handoff.mode_preservation: Retain 100755 versus 100644 through publication and relation review even if legacy code payload capture stores only text bytes. A capture that drops mode/type loses proof and must not be upgraded to official source evidence.
source_handoff.handoff_refusal: No handoff for symlinks, submodules, trees, unsupported modes, incomplete observations, normalized-only content, invalid UTF-8 text, raw-byte mismatch, or an unbound host assertion when repository binding is required.

config_evidence.raw_binding: Every config record names the observation/target, blob_oid, raw_sha256, size_bytes, parser_profile_sha256 and exact source bytes. A config record from a normalized view is insufficient.

span_record.coordinate_rule: Byte offsets and columns are computed against the exact raw UTF-8 bytes; line ranges use the existing UTF-8 LF normalization. byte_end is exclusive and every offset/range must be within the blob.
span_record.verification_rule: The public verifier slices the retained raw bytes and recomputes raw_span_sha256. It recomputes the normalized line digest with the existing code snippet rule. Caller-provided excerpts are advisory and never replace these checks.
span_record.semantic_rule: JSON pointers use RFC 6901 escaping; TOML key paths are ordered key components. The span must resolve to the parser node/value named by the path; key/value spans are retained separately when required. Span lists are canonical sorted and bounded.

config_evidence.json_profile: Strict UTF-8, no BOM, RFC 8259 whitespace, no duplicate keys, no floats/NaN/Infinity under the current safe profile, no trailing data, bounded depth/nodes/string/bytes, and a span-producing tokenizer cross-checked against the parsed data. stdlib JSON parsing alone is insufficient because it does not provide trusted node spans.
config_evidence.toml_profile: Bounded TOML data-only parsing with duplicate-key and syntax rejection, no imports/interpolation/object constructors/scripts, supported scalar/table/array types frozen explicitly, and a span-producing lexer cross-checked against the parsed data. tomllib may validate data syntax but its returned values alone do not provide exact source spans.
config_evidence.claim_rule: Capability or mismatch claims cite exact verified spans and source hash. A missing key is only an observed absence when the requested config inventory and bounded search scope are complete; an unfetched file remains unverified.

budgets.status: Prospective starting profile for Architect freeze; every value must be copied into the request and charged before observation installation. No silent truncation.
budgets.charging: Count request targets and declared object records before reading bodies; charge each retained body and span bytes before allocation/publication; limit overflow is a typed refusal. The existing 64 MiB code payload ceiling remains the hard per-source cap unless a successor explicitly changes it.

error_taxonomy.case: Noncanonical JSON, unknown field, duplicate key, missing required object, invalid path, symlinked bundle component, compressed/archived transport, or manifest digest mismatch.
Body size, body_sha256, framed_sha256, selected-format Git OID, type, or object header does not agree.
Mixed SHA-1/SHA-256 objects, short/uppercase OID, wrong OID length, or an untyped compatibility OID is used as primary identity.
Commit tree header, root tree, intermediate tree path walk, tree entry mode/name/OID, or canonical tree body is inconsistent.
Omitted, duplicate, extra, reordered-without-canonicalization, or differently scoped target record.
Per-file observations disagree on repository, object format, commit, root tree, request, bundle snapshot, or retained generation.
Bundle root/object replacement, disappearance, mode/identity/size/byte change, unsafe component, or directory generation race.
Hosting assertion disagrees with the self-consistent bundle repository or commit. A self-consistent unbound bundle remains non-official evidence.
Symlink, submodule/gitlink, tree target, unsupported mode, executable role violation, path traversal, or unsafe type.
Normalized-only text, metadata-only result, invalid source text, raw byte mismatch, or missing mode/type proof is offered for source handoff.
Unsupported format, duplicate key, parser construct, limit overflow, trailing data, span outside bytes, span digest mismatch, or span/value path disagreement.
A SHA-256 commit is forced into the 40-hex legacy code-evidence-manifest.v1 origin.
A partial target set or missing/inaccessible target is published or handed off as complete.

acceptance_cases: A local SHA-1 bundle with one commit, root tree, path-walk trees and two blobs verifies framed Git object hashes, raw SHA-256 bytes and complete same-commit target membership.
A local SHA-256 bundle verifies 64-hex commit/tree/blob identities and remains distinct from ordinary body SHA-256; no field truncation or SHA-1 substitution occurs.
Mutating only the hosting assertion changes its assertion digest and repository-binding result while leaving self-consistent object proofs unchanged; the result is not officiality.
One observation over several targets fails closed when an object file or bundle directory is replaced between target scans; separate per-file calls cannot split one observation across lineages.
An absent target retains the deepest proven tree edge and bounded inventory scope; an extra/omitted/duplicate target is rejected before installation.
Equal blob bytes at two distinct paths remain two target records, two exact tree walks and two logical origin paths.

A mode-100755 implementation/entrypoint source succeeds when explicitly permitted, while the same mode at an unpermitted role, mode-120000 symlink, mode-160000 submodule, and requested tree each refuse without dereference.
CRLF source preserves raw_sha256 and blob OID while normalized line metadata and line-span digest follow existing UTF-8-LF rules.
A normalized-only provider excerpt cannot create a byte-verified handoff or Git source manifest.
A SHA-256 source target refuses legacy code-evidence-manifest.v1 with CODE_PROOF_LEGACY_COMMIT_UNREPRESENTABLE and remains available for a successor/raw-capture-only path.
Malformed tree ordering, duplicate tree names, wrong parent tree, forged path, wrong blob OID, wrong body length and mixed object formats each produce the named typed refusal.

JSON duplicate keys, BOM, floats/NaN, trailing bytes, deep/nodal overflow, and TOML duplicate/unsupported constructs refuse without execution; valid JSON/TOML spans are checked from raw byte offsets and normalized line hashes.
Source code imports contain no subprocess/socket/urllib/Git invocation for bundle validation; public tests prove zero network, zero process spawn and no real-Vault write.

proposed_files.ownership_note: Prospective paths only. Connector transport, hosting assertions, external Git object acquisition and human relation review remain outside public Python. Any v2 legacy-manifest schema requires a separate Architect freeze and compatibility review.

blockers: Freeze whether v1 will include a new SHA-256-capable code-evidence manifest/binding. Existing code-evidence-manifest.v1 hard-codes a 40-hex commit, so accepting SHA-256 proof without a successor would create a false binding.

Freeze the exact local uncompressed bundle directory digest algorithm, raw-object record schema, tree canonicalization rules, retained descriptor/snapshot implementation and hosting-assertion status semantics before Builder writes.

Freeze a span-producing JSON/TOML parser profile. stdlib JSON and tomllib can validate data but do not alone expose trusted exact node spans; line numbers supplied by a connector are not evidence until raw-byte slices are recomputed.
Actual provider/repository observations, officiality relation judgments, and human publication gates remain open and are not established by this design review.
